text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it disputed the extent of the 631 million mark loss reported by Grundig AG earlier this week.

Philips is obliged to cover Grundig's losses up to the end of 1996, but a spokesman said Philips would not pay up in full until it had agreed with Grundig on a "reasonable amount" for the German firm's 1996 loss.
Philips said in January it planned to reduce its role in Grundig to that of a passive 32 percent shareholder and from this year would no longer bear 100 percent of Grundig's losses.
"We have paid 225 million marks in advance but we will not pay any more until we have agreed with Grundig AG on what is a reasonable amount," Philips spokesman Ben Geerts said.

Despite its minority holding, Philips assumed management control over Grundig under a 1984 agreement under which it also undertook to cover any losses which Grundig made. Philips says it lost over 1.5 billion marks on the deal over 12 years.
Additionally Philips committed itself to pay an annual dividend of 45 million marks to the majority shareholder -- the Max Grundig Foundation -- whether Grundig made a profit or not.
Geerts said Philips had recently honoured another contractual obligation to buy a 16 percent stake in Grundig from the foundation at a price of 129 million marks.
This had then been sold on -- at a lower price -- to a Cologne-based asset management firm called Hohenstaufen.
Geerts declined to specify the loss which Philips had made on this deal, but he said it had been covered by provisions which were charged against Philips' 1996 results.
He said Philips was still pursuing talks aimed at buying off the foundation's right to sell its remaining 52 percent Grundig stake to Philips in 2004 for 411 million marks.
Geerts said Philips was hopeful it could resolve all outstanding matters with Grundig and the foundation amicably.
